question: What is the primary purpose of a dietary assessment in clinical nursing?

options.A: Evaluating an individual's food and nutrient intake
options.B: Calculating the exact daily hospital food budget
options.C: Determining the patient's exact genetic metabolic rate
options.D: Prescribing specialized surgical diets without a doctor

explanation: Dietary assessment systematically measures what a person eats to understand their baseline nutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h1)

question: Why is dietary assessment particularly crucial during initial nursing admissions?

options.A: It eliminates all risks of hospital-acquired infections
options.B: It guarantees the patient will follow hospital routines
options.C: It replaces the need for standard anthropometric measurements
options.D: It uncovers hidden nutrient deficits before physical symptoms appear

explanation: Catching inadequate intake early helps prevent full-blown malnutrition during a hospital stay. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h1)

question: Monitoring a therapeutic diet over time is a key objective of which nursing activity?
explanation: Tracking food intake helps nurses see if a prescribed therapeutic diet is working. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h2)

question: How does dietary evaluation support community health epidemiology?

options.A: Determining the cost of pharmaceutical drugs nationwide
options.B: Treating acute malaria outbreaks in rural health posts
options.C: Linking food patterns to chronic diseases in populations
options.D: Mapping out safe drinking water sources in villages

explanation: Population-level dietary data helps researchers connect eating habits to disease trends. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h2)

question: What does a 24-hour dietary recall method require a patient to do?

options.A: Write down every ingredient before cooking a pot of soup
options.B: Report all foods and beverages consumed over the past day
options.C: Fast completely for a full day before laboratory blood tests
options.D: Weigh every single meal on a scale for an entire week

explanation: A 24-hour recall asks the patient to list everything eaten during the previous day. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h3)

question: A major drawback of retrospective dietary methods is their reliance on what factor?
explanation: Since retrospective methods look backward, they depend entirely on what the patient can remember. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h3)

question: What is the primary characteristic of a prospective dietary assessment method?

options.A: Recording food intake as it happens in real time
options.B: Recalling meals eaten during childhood years
options.C: Estimating food portions five years after discharge
options.D: Guessing nutrient intake based on blood test results

explanation: Prospective methods capture data at the exact moment of consumption to avoid memory lapses. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h4)

question: Why can weighed food records be difficult to use in busy clinical wards?

options.A: They require continuous intravenous fluid therapy
options.B: They only work for patients who are completely blind
options.C: They place a high burden on staff and patients
options.D: They cannot be calculated using local food tables

explanation: Weighing every single item and leftover demands significant time and effort from patients and nurses. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h4)

question: What does the acronym RDA stand for in nutritional assessment?
explanation: RDA stands for Recommended Dietary Allowance, representing intake levels that meet nearly all healthy individuals' needs. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h5)

question: Which DRI parameter represents the highest daily nutrient intake unlikely to cause harm?
explanation: The Tolerable Upper Intake Level defines the safe threshold before nutrient toxicity occurs. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h5)

question: Why do patients sometimes misreport their food intake during dietary assessments?

options.A: They want to impress the nurse with healthy choices
options.B: They want to speed up intravenous fluid removal
options.C: They are trying to reduce hospital admission fees
options.D: They are required by law to hide their recipes

explanation: Social desirability bias causes patients to underreport unhealthy items and exaggerate healthy ones. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h6)

question: Which factor makes assessing mixed Nigerian dishes particularly challenging?

options.A: Lack of any standard kitchen utensils throughout the country
options.B: The complete absence of local vegetables in traditional markets
options.C: Difficulty in measuring precise ingredient proportions in a shared pot
options.D: Strict legal regulations forbidding the analysis of soups

explanation: Mixed dishes contain varied ingredients cooked together, making exact nutrient breakdowns hard to calculate. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h6)

question: A patient's dietary record reveals extreme nutrient deficiencies. What is the appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Scold the patient for eating poor quality food at home
options.B: Collaborate with the dietitian to formulate a culturally appropriate meal plan
options.C: Discharge the patient immediately without further nutritional support
options.D: Stop all medication administration and start strict bed rest

explanation: Nurses use assessment findings to collaborate on practical, culturally relevant nutritional interventions. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h7)

question: How does the evaluation phase tie back into the initial dietary assessment?

options.A: By rewriting the hospital budget for kitchen supplies
options.B: By checking if weight changes and lab values show improvement
options.C: By closing the patient file and stopping all nursing notes
options.D: By ensuring the patient never eats local food again

explanation: Evaluating the care plan requires measuring clinical outcomes against baseline dietary data. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h7)
